messages:
alex: Heads-up — we see a quality regression after the FP8 rollout on gptq-4k. Eval set delta: +6% hallucination rate, structured JSON outputs occasionally truncated.

marta: Oof. When did the rollout start?

alex: rolled at 02:30 UTC (canary -> 10% -> 50%). Spike correlates with the 50% step.

sam: Any perf telemetry? latency/cpu/gpu changes?

alex: Perf shows a GPU kernel switch and increased KV cache misses around the same time. Profiling snippet: 
```
2026-03-15T02:50Z profile summary:
- avg_latency +12ms
- tokens/sec -8%
- kv_hit_rate 82% -> 69%
- kernel: fp8_stitch_v2 used 78% of calls (was 6% before)
- batching: handshake time +4.2ms median
```

eva: fp8_stitch_v2 was the new kernel we shipped for latency savings on long context, but it had simplified KV index arithmetic (to vectorize). Could cause alignment mismatches with mixed-precision keys.

chris: Do we have repro locally with the canary config? If KV index math off-by-one that's a deterministic bug.

alex: Repro is intermittent — appears mostly on prompts that trigger early stop tokens and structured JSON outputs. Repro steps attached (short prompt + output schema).

marta: Might be a rounding/calibration mismatch between fp8 quant and the cached KV (stored as int8 on-disk). If cache keys quantized differently at write vs read you get misses and then fallbacks to a different generation path -> hallucination.

sam: Quick mitigation: pin kernel to fp8_compat_v1 or roll back canary to INT8 variant for affected model. Which is easier?

eva: Pinning kernel per-model is quick in the runtime config. Rollback is slower for traffic shifting. I'd vote pin + disable the new batching handshake for the model.

alex: Agree. I'll open a hotfix: set kernel_override to fp8_compat_v1, kv_compat_mode=true, and batching.handshake=false for gptq-4k on canary.

infra-bot: deploy request created #DR-4521 by alex; priority P1; target: canary patch; ETA 12m.

rollout-bot: canary traffic adjusted to 10% after patch.

chris: On the investigative side we need: deterministic repro, microtrace of KV key encoding path (write vs read), and kernel microbench comparing fp8_stitch_v2 vs fp8_compat_v1 on identical inputs. Sam/Eva can you run nvprof/perf and the runtime event traces?

sam: On it — will push a perf job with 1000 short-schema prompts. Expect traces in ~20m.

eva: I'll instrument KV encode/decode to dump key fingerprints (sha1 of pre-quant) for a sample. If write/read use different quant scale we will see mismatched fingerprints.

marta: Also check calibration table used during quantization. There was a small change to the activation histogram smoothing for fp8 in the last model packaging pipeline. If the scale table changed, that can shift index distribution.

alex: Adding list of immediate action items: 
- [x] runtime pin & handshake disable (alex)
- [ ] perf traces & microbench (sam)
- [ ] KV fingerprint dumps (eva)
- [ ] compare calibration tables between v1/v2 packages (marta)
- [ ] run eval harness on pinned config to confirm delta resolved (chris)

chris: If all that passes, we can re-enable fp8_stitch_v2 behind a stricter KV-consistency check and a calibration-validated rollout.

alex: Thanks — I'll monitor canary evals and post updates here. :thumbsup:

(edited)
